newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan envoy plans damage-control Guatemala visit.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan envoy plans damage-control Guatemala visit.

text.p: Taiwan, under constant diplomatic pressure from rival China, said on Monday it would send its top envoy to Guatemala for the December 29 signing of a peace pact between the Guatemalan government and leftist rebels.
Foreign Minister John Chang said he would attend the ceremony on behalf of President Lee Teng-hui, but described his trip as a "simple visit" that did not include side trips to other countries.
"The trip is still being finalised, but right now there are no plans to visit other countries," Chang was quoted by the state-run Central News Agency as saying.

The trip is one of four foreign damage-control missions planned by Taiwan officials since Taipei's largest ally, South Africa, shocked the island in November by announcing it would switch ties to Beijing by the end of 1997.
Taipei acknowledges that it is threatened by China's long-standing drive to isolate Taiwan from international arenas until it can be reunified under mainland sovereignty.
China has regarded Taiwan as a renegade province since a civil war split them in 1949.

Guatemala, ravaged by its own civil war in the past 36 years, is one of only 30 countries that recognise Taiwan's exiled Republic of China government instead of the communist Chinese government in Beijing.
Chang visited South Africa in December in a failed attempt to rescue ties and will return to Pretoria in January along with visits to several neigbouring African countries.
Vice-President Lien Chan will visit Nicaragua, a Taipei ally, in January for the inauguration of President-elect Arnoldo Aleman.
Most of Taiwan's allies are underdeveloped states in Africa and central America.
